title: Generative AI, Language Models, and Agent Fundamentals

cards.question: What does generative AI do in response to a prompt?
cards.answer: Creates original content in response to the prompt.

cards.question: What is an AI agent?
cards.answer: An AI application that can perform tasks on behalf of a user.

cards.question: An AI application reads an email aloud. Which speech capability is it using?
What is a large language model (LLM) designed to generate?
What is the purpose of tokenization?
cards.answer: To break text into smaller units called tokens.

cards.question: What are token embeddings?
cards.answer: Vector-based representations of tokens that capture their semantic meaning.

cards.question: What does an attention layer examine in a transformer model?
cards.answer: The relationships between each token and the tokens around it.

cards.question: What is the purpose of a system prompt?
cards.answer: To provide context and instructions to the AI model.

cards.question: How do tokenization and embeddings differ?
cards.answer: Tokenization splits text into units; embeddings represent tokens as semantic vectors.

cards.question: How does an AI agent differ from a large language model (LLM)?
cards.answer: An agent performs tasks for a user; an LLM is designed to generate human-like text.
